scope: Independent falsification of newest complete eligible T0 work under hard downstream backpressure. No fresh names opened. TER and SERV challenged against current exact gates without converting plausible future risks into blockers.
summary: Red-team challenge did not falsify either structural thesis, but it preserves the distinction between opportunity and investable capture. TER's historical convertible/warrant complex must not be misrepresented as current dilution; the real live challenge is current SBC/debt/repurchase normalization plus concentration/cycle exposure. SERV's $79.112M Q2 cash anchor cannot be treated as runway proof until operating cash use, equity capacity and concentration are extracted. These are exact underwriting gates for Deep Resolver, not invented Beta blockers.

claims: A bearish case based on Teradyne's old 1.25% convertible notes or associated warrants as current dilution is stale: the notes matured in 2023 and warrants expired by July 2024.

The valid present challenge is whether 2026 SBC/current debt/repurchase behavior offsets operating strength and whether AI/customer concentration makes apparent diversification less resilient than headline segment breadth suggests.
risks: Current SBC may dilute owners even though legacy convertibles are extinguished.
Customer and AI-capex concentration can make earnings more fragile than segment labels imply.
Repurchases can be value-destructive if used mainly to mask SBC or executed at poor prices.
contradictions: Legacy convertible/warrant risk appearing as current exposure is contradicted by primary filings showing maturity/expiry.
unknowns: 2026 SBC/unvested awards, fully diluted share count, current debt and executed repurchases.
evidence.exactGate: Current 2026 SBC/governance dilution, current debt and executed repurchases are not yet normalized reproducibly; historical convertibles/warrants must be excluded.
evidence.nextLawfulSourcePath: Teradyne 2026 definitive proxy equity-compensation tables plus latest 2026 Form 10-Q debt/equity/share-count and repurchase disclosures.

claims: Serve's June 30, 2026 cash balance is a point-in-time liquidity fact, not a runway conclusion.
Partner/category expansion can reduce use-case dependence but cannot be counted as diversification quality until revenue concentration and recurring paid-volume economics are known.
The strongest present falsification path is financing/runway and concentration, not speculative claims that sidewalk autonomy has no market.
risks: Cash fell from $106.239M at 2025 year-end to $79.112M at June 30, 2026; without H1 operating cash use, runway cannot be inferred.
ATM, warrants and SBC can transfer a meaningful portion of future upside away from current owners.
Customer/platform concentration can create bargaining-power and demand fragility despite expansion announcements.
contradictions: Any treatment of the Q2 cash balance alone as proof of adequate runway would exceed the evidence.
unknowns: H1 operating cash use, unused ATM capacity, warrant/SBC overhang, partner/customer concentration and recurring paid-volume economics.
evidence.exactGate: Q2 2026 operating cash use, current equity/ATM capacity, warrant/SBC overhang and customer/partner concentration remain unextracted, preventing reproducible survival/dilution/concentration treatment.
evidence.nextLawfulSourcePath: Serve Robotics Q2 2026 Form 10-Q cash-flow statement and equity/warrant, revenue/customer concentration and commitments notes; incorporated ATM prospectus only for residual capacity detail.

blockingIssues.nextLawfulSourcePath: Q2 2026 10-Q notes and incorporated ATM prospectus if needed.
